10.1.crux: Adolescence is the time, roughly from 11 to 18 or 19 years, when the body changes towards adulthood; puberty is the main change that makes it able to reproduce.

cards.title: Growing up in stages
say: Adolescence is the period between childhood and adulthood.
Because it covers ages 13 to 19 ('teens'), it is often called teenage.

cards.title: Puberty

steps.text: Puberty begins: the body starts changing
Many changes in size, shape, voice and feelings
Puberty ends when the body can reproduce

say: Puberty is the most important change of adolescence.
It may start a year or two earlier in girls than in boys.
cards.remember: Adolescence = the years of change; puberty = the changes that make the body able to reproduce.

cards.title: Everyone is different

items.sub: Ask parents, teachers or a doctor

say: There's no single 'right' age for these changes.
It is normal for friends to change at different times.

crux_points: Adolescence is roughly ages 11 to 18 or 19.
Puberty is the set of changes that make the body able to reproduce.
These changes happen at different times for different people.

options: The body becomes able to reproduce
quiz.why: Puberty ends when reproductive maturity is reached.

options: It covers the years ending in 'teen'
quiz.why: Thirteen to nineteen are the 'teen' years.

10.2.crux: At puberty you grow taller, your body shape and voice change, sweat and oil glands become more active, and you mature in mind and feelings too.

cards.title: Changes at puberty

items.sub: Long bones of the arms and legs grow
Boys' shoulders broaden; girls' hips widen

say: The sudden increase in height is one of the most noticeable changes.
At first, arms and legs may seem out of proportion; the body catches up soon.

cards.title: The voice box
say: In boys the voice box grows larger and can be seen as a bump on the throat called the Adam's apple.
Boys' voices become deeper; girls' voices stay high-pitched.
cards.remember: Adam's apple = a bigger voice box.

cards.title: Pimples are common

steps.text: Sweat and oil glands become more active
Many young people get pimples (acne)
Wash your face regularly to keep skin clean

say: Pimples are a normal part of growing up.

cards.title: Organs and feelings

items.sub: Testes and penis in boys; ovaries enlarge in girls

say: Adolescents may feel unsure at times. Talking to trusted adults helps.

crux_points: Height increases and body shape changes.
The voice box grows: boys develop an Adam's apple and a deeper voice.
Sweat and oil glands become active; the mind and feelings mature too.

options: A larger voice box seen in boys' throats
quiz.why: At puberty boys' larynx grows and shows as a bump on the throat.

quiz.q: Why do many adolescents get pimples?
options: Oil and sweat glands become more active
quiz.why: More active oil glands can block the skin and cause acne.

10.3.crux: Secondary sexual characters, like a beard in boys and breasts in girls, help tell males and females apart; hormones testosterone and estrogen cause them.

cards.title: Secondary sexual characters

cols.head: Boys
cells: Hair on chest, armpits, pubic area

cols.head: Girls
cells: Hair in armpits and pubic area

say: These features help us distinguish a male from a female.
They are called secondary sexual characters.

cards.title: Hormones cause them

cols.head: Testosterone
cells: Beard, deep voice and other male features

say: Hormones are chemical messengers.
At puberty the testes and ovaries start making these hormones.
cards.remember: Testosterone in boys; estrogen in girls.

cards.title: Primary and secondary

items.sub: Other features that develop at puberty

say: Secondary characters are not needed for reproduction itself, but they mark the body's maturity.

crux_points: Secondary sexual characters develop at puberty and differ in boys and girls.
Testosterone (from testes) causes male features.
Estrogen (from ovaries) causes female features.

quiz.q: Which hormone causes boys to grow a beard?
quiz.why: Testosterone, made by the testes, causes male secondary sexual characters.
The ovaries make estrogen, the female hormone.

10.4.crux: Hormones are chemical messengers made by endocrine glands and carried by the blood; the pituitary gland signals the testes and ovaries to start working at puberty.

cards.title: Endocrine glands

labels.name: Pituitary
labels.note: Below the brain: controls other glands

say: Endocrine glands release hormones straight into the blood.
They have no tubes (ducts), so they are also called ductless glands.

cards.title: How a hormone works

steps.text: A gland releases a hormone
The blood carries it around the body
It acts on a particular target organ

say: A hormone is like a message posted through the bloodstream to one address.

cards.title: Starting puberty

steps.text: Pituitary gland releases a hormone
It reaches the testes or ovaries
They begin making testosterone or estrogen
Puberty changes begin

say: So the pituitary gland is the starter switch for puberty.

crux_points: Hormones are chemical messengers released into the blood.
Endocrine (ductless) glands make hormones.
The pituitary signals the testes and ovaries to make sex hormones.

quiz.why: The pituitary sits just below the brain and controls other glands.

quiz.q: How do hormones reach their target organs?
quiz.why: Endocrine glands release hormones directly into the bloodstream.

10.5.crux: In humans the reproductive phase starts at puberty; in women an egg matures about once a month, and if it isn't fertilised the uterus lining is shed in menstruation.

cards.title: The reproductive phase
say: In women this phase lasts from about 10–12 years to about 45–50 years.
In men it usually lasts much longer.

cards.title: The monthly cycle

steps.text: Every 28 to 30 days, one egg matures and is released by an ovary.
The wall of the uterus thickens, ready to receive a fertilised egg.
If the egg isn't fertilised, the egg and thick lining come out with blood.
The cycle begins again, controlled by hormones.

say: This monthly flow is called menstruation.
cards.remember: Menarche: first menstruation. Menopause: when it stops.

cards.title: Two milestones
say: Menstruation is a natural, healthy process.
Cleanliness during this time is very important.

crux_points: The reproductive phase begins at puberty.
About every 28–30 days an egg is released; if not fertilised, menstruation follows.
Menarche is the first menstruation; menopause is when it stops.

quiz.q: The first menstrual flow is called…
quiz.why: Menarche is the first menstruation, at puberty.
If the egg isn't fertilised, the thickened lining of the uterus is shed.

10.6.crux: Every egg carries an X chromosome; the sperm carries either X or Y; X+X gives a girl and X+Y gives a boy, so the father's sperm decides the baby's sex.

cards.title: Sex chromosomes

cols.head: Male
cells: One X and one Y chromosome

say: Our cells have 23 pairs of chromosomes.
Two of them, X and Y, are the sex chromosomes.

cards.title: Who decides: girl or boy?
say: Every egg has an X chromosome.
A sperm can carry either an X or a Y chromosome.
cards.remember: The father's sperm (X or Y) decides whether the baby is a girl or a boy.

cards.title: Busting a myth

cols.head: Myth
cells: The mother decides if the baby is a boy or girl

cols.head: Fact
cells: It depends on whether the sperm carries X or Y; the mother can't decide it

say: Blaming mothers for the sex of a baby is wrong and unscientific.

crux_points: Females have XX and males have XY sex chromosomes.
Every egg has X; a sperm has X or Y.
X sperm gives a girl (XX), Y sperm gives a boy (XY): the mother is not responsible.

quiz.q: An egg is fertilised by a sperm carrying Y. The baby will be…
Which chromosome does every egg carry?
quiz.why: Females are XX, so every egg has an X.

10.7.crux: Besides sex hormones, endocrine glands make thyroxine (thyroid), insulin (pancreas), adrenalin (adrenal) and growth hormone (pituitary).

cards.title: Glands and their hormones
say: Each gland makes its own hormones for particular jobs.

cards.title: Where they are
say: The pituitary also controls the other glands, so it is called the master gland.

cards.title: Adrenalin in action

steps.text: You feel angry, scared or stressed
Adrenal glands release adrenalin into the blood
Heart beats faster, breathing speeds up: the body is ready to act

say: Adrenalin helps the body adjust to stress, anger, worry or embarrassment.

crux_points: Thyroid makes thyroxine; too little causes goitre.
Pancreas makes insulin; too little causes diabetes.
Adrenal glands make adrenalin for stress; the pituitary makes growth hormone and controls other glands.

quiz.q: Which hormone does the pancreas make?
quiz.why: The pancreas makes insulin; lack of insulin causes diabetes.

quiz.q: Goitre is linked to which gland?
quiz.why: Goitre happens when the thyroid doesn't make enough thyroxine.

10.8.crux: Hormones control metamorphosis: in frogs, thyroxine turns a tadpole into an adult, and the thyroid needs iodine in the water to make it.

cards.title: Tadpole to frog

steps.text: Frog eggs are laid in water.
Tadpoles hatch; they swim with tails.
Thyroxine makes legs grow and the tail shrink.
An adult frog that can live on land.

say: The change from tadpole to frog is metamorphosis.
It is controlled by the hormone thyroxine.

cards.title: Iodine is needed
say: If the water lacks iodine, tadpoles can't become adult frogs.
cards.remember: No iodine → no thyroxine → no metamorphosis.

cards.title: Insects too

steps.text: Egg
Larva (caterpillar)
Pupa
Adult

say: Insect metamorphosis is also controlled by insect hormones.

cards.title: Iodine for people

items.sub: Gives us the iodine our thyroid needs
The thyroid can't make enough thyroxine (goitre)

say: That's why salt sold in India has iodine added to it.

crux_points: Metamorphosis is the change from larva to adult.
In frogs, thyroxine controls metamorphosis.
Thyroxine needs iodine; without iodine tadpoles can't become frogs.

quiz.q: Which hormone turns a tadpole into a frog?
quiz.why: Thyroxine from the thyroid controls frog metamorphosis.

quiz.q: Tadpoles in water without iodine will…
quiz.why: Without iodine the thyroid can't make thyroxine.

10.9.crux: To stay healthy as you grow, eat a balanced diet, keep clean, exercise, and say no to drugs.

cards.title: A balanced diet
say: Your body is growing fast, so it needs plenty of good food.
Iron helps build blood; growing girls especially need iron-rich food.

cards.title: Keep clean, keep active

items.sub: Sweat glands are more active now
Walks and games keep body and mind fit

say: Girls should take special care of cleanliness during menstruation.

cards.title: Say NO to drugs

steps.text: Drugs are addictive: once taken, the body wants more
They harm the body and mind
Sharing syringes for drugs can spread HIV, which causes AIDS

say: If anyone offers you drugs, say no and tell a trusted adult.
cards.remember: Drugs give no benefit, only harm.

cards.title: Myths vs facts

cols.head: Myth
cells: Girls shouldn't work in the kitchen during menstruation
The mother decides a baby's sex

cols.head: Fact
cells: There is no reason for this
The father's sperm (X or Y) decides

say: Ask a teacher or doctor if you hear something that worries you.

crux_points: Eat a balanced diet with protein, iron and vitamins.
Keep clean and exercise regularly.
Say no to drugs; they are addictive and harmful.

quiz.q: Which food is rich in iron?
quiz.why: Leafy vegetables, jaggery and amla are good sources of iron.

quiz.q: Why should adolescents say no to drugs?
options: Drugs are addictive and harm body and mind
quiz.why: Drugs are addictive and damage health.
